reconcile.connective: Matthew Henry reads the veil's tearing as coinciding with Christ's last breath rather than following it, so the Gospels' differing placement records one simultaneous event, not a strict sequence.

discrepancy.connective: Bart Ehrman presses the sequence as unresolvable on the page: Mark has the curtain tear only after Jesus dies, Luke has it tear while he is still alive, and for Ehrman the two accounts simply cannot both be right.

skeptic.name: Bart D. Ehrman
skeptic.work: Jesus, Interrupted: Revealing the Hidden Contradictions in the Bible (And Why We Don't Know About Them)
skeptic.attribution: Bart D. Ehrman, Jesus, Interrupted: Revealing the Hidden Contradictions in the Bible (And Why We Don't Know About Them) (HarperOne, 2009), pp. 51-52

excerpts.excerpt_text: Just at that instant that Christ died upon mount Calvary, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom, Mar 15:38.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Henry states the veil tore 'just at that instant' Christ died, treating the two events as simultaneous rather than as strictly sequential — directly answers the Luke-vs-Matthew/Mark ordering tension.

pd_work.resource: Matthew Henry, Commentary on the Whole Bible (1706-1714)
pd_work.author: Matthew Henry
pd_work.note: Henry treats this exact scene, reading the veil's tearing as simultaneous with Christ's death rather than sequential to it. (Haley's Alleged Discrepancies does not treat this specific verse pair; no 'veil'/'curtain' entry on the crucifixion sequence was found in the 1874 text.)
